due_when.clears_when: The `diag_log_name` signal reports the LOG'S OWN STATE, not the allowlist's — i.e. it grades `present` from /api/diag/log_file?name=<n> (three states, never collapsed: `present_with_rows` / `present_empty` / `absent`, plus `could_not_look` when the diag read fails, since an unreachable VM is not evidence a file is missing), and only `present_with_rows` counts toward `likely_met`. VERIFIED by re-running backlog_drain_candidates.py and observing BL-20260830-BUILDER-EXCEPTION-LATCH-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-WRITTEN drop OUT of `likely_met` while at least one row whose log genuinely carries rows stays IN — both halves, because a signal that now matches nothing is not a fix. ⚠️ If a live diag read is judged too expensive for this tool to make, the acceptable alternative is to RENAME the signal to say what it actually checks (e.g. `diag_name_allowlisted`) and stop counting it toward `likely_met` on its own — but silently keeping a presence check under a name that reads as an observation is not.
